claim: Default LLMs asked to test a hypothesis choose mostly confirming tests (incompatible-to-compatible ratio below 1 in all 11 models tested), and success on 2-4-6-style rule discovery tracks the share of disconfirming tests.
agent_test: Run Wason-style and FalsifyBench tasks with and without a forced disconfirm step at equal tokens; log I:C.
audit_note: I:C below 1 in all 11 models (Table 2) and positive I:C-success correlation verified in the Jhaveri html; FalsifyBench independently supports negative-testing-drives-success.

claim: Prompting to test the opposite (Think-in-Opposites) lifts rule discovery from 42% to 56% on average and improved all 11 model-by-mode settings; gains are significant for thinking models and mixed for non-thinking ones; Dual-Goal helps less.
agent_test: Add a one-line opposite-test instruction to S7; compare success per token with plain and best-of-N.

claim: Reasoning models falsify more and succeed more: FalsifyBench success 75% (GPT-5.2-Chat) and 68% (GPT-OSS-120B) against 33-41% for instruction-tuned models; confirmation bias strongly predicts failure (odds ratio 0.016, n=1,200 games).
agent_test: Evaluate the scaffold on a FalsifyBench subset against a reasoning-mode baseline at equal tokens.

claim: On WILT (2024 models) the best model reached only 28% (14/50), and on FalsifyBench (2026) the best instruction-tuned model reached 41% while reasoning models did better (GPT-5.2-Chat 75%, GPT-OSS-120B 68%); both benchmarks show hypothesis-testing weakness, strongest in non-reasoning models.
agent_test: Run WILT with the scaffold; track guesses used.
audit_note: FalsifyBench's 41% is only for instruction-tuned models; its reasoning models reach 75% (GPT-5.2-Chat) and 68%, and WILT tested 2024 models (best 28%), so 'frontier LLMs stay weak, a consistent gap across two benchmarks' is too strong.
claim_before_audit: Frontier LLMs stay weak at multi-turn rule induction (WILT 2024: best 14/50; FalsifyBench 2026: instruction-tuned at most 41%), a consistent capability gap across two benchmarks.

claim: Agreeable AI partners cut human discovery of a hidden rule: default GPT 5.9% vs 29.5% for unbiased sampling (difference 23.6 points, 504 participants with a hypothesis, 557 recruited); confirming AI also raises confidence. Gap search: the 29.5% came from random hypothesis-independent sequences; AI told to disconfirm reached only 14.1%.
agent_test: Seed the agent with a user hypothesis and check whether its self-chosen tests fall below unbiased sampling.

claim: Training students on traces made under falsification-promoting interventions raises Wason success (8B almost tripled) with small math transfer (8B AIME 2025 0.60 vs 0.33), not significant at 32B.
agent_test: Not testable in a scaffold-only agent; record as an upper bound.

claim: Teaching founders to treat strategy as hypothesis testing raised pivoting (41 pivots, 30 firms) and cross-section revenue in 116 startups; a pooled replication of 759 firms across four RCTs is reported robust (working paper). Replication is a published SMJ 2024 article (abstract read: 759 firms, more terminated ideas, nonlinear pivots); revenue effects unchecked.
agent_test: Not directly testable; motivation for a hypothesis-then-test loop.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Revenue effects of the scientific-approach training are fragile to specification: panel linear 674.97 (p=0.127) not significant, winsorized 172.5 (p=0.037), sinh cross-section p=0.065.
agent_test: Treat the effect as moderate when citing value of assumption testing.

claim: A/B testing adoption among 35,262 startups goes with about 8.5-11.8% more page views after controls (280% raw), concentrated in firms older than about 5 years, and 9-18% more product launches; observational.
agent_test: Compare a cheap-experiment step vs none on planning tasks.

claim: An LLM business adviser did not help on average (+0.05 s.d., CI -0.06 to 0.16) but split by baseline: high performers about +15%, low performers about -10% (gap 0.267 s.d., p=0.013); low performers adopted generic advice.
agent_test: Check that the agent asks for the riskiest assumption instead of giving generic advice; compare advice specificity.

claim: LLM self-correction without external feedback does not help and often lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0), while an oracle signal helps. Assumption checks need discriminating external evidence, not re-reading.
agent_test: Compare an internal-review step with a tool-grounded test at equal tokens.

claim: Information-gain querying is not always best: it can hurt on simple concepts through a support-mismatch trap where positive tests converge faster; BoxingGym found model-based design augmentation did not reliably help. Gap search: on easy rules positive tests converge as fast or faster; on compound rules information-gain queries win (Number Game, Gemini 2.5 Flash).
agent_test: Compare a mix of positive and boundary tests against pure disconfirmation on simple and complex rules.

claim: Verification before acting improves agent outcomes in several 2026 benchmarks, for example a static verifier catches 95.8% of invalid shell commands at 10.0% false positives, and removing verification raised ALFWorld failures from 2 to 9.
agent_test: Add a pre-commit assumption check; measure failures and replans at equal tokens.
audit_note: Both numbers verified (95.8% at 10.0% FPR; failures 2 to 9 in ALFWorld ablation), but the ablation is one run on 134 tasks with unclear count-vs-percent units, and the shell result measures detection, not downstream agent outcome.

claim: Closed-loop active experimentation lifts discovery (NewtonBench symbolic accuracy 67.6% vs below 8% for LLM baselines); preprint results only.
agent_test: Compare an experiment-proposal step with passive reasoning on a small simulator.

claim: No controlled study was found of LLM-generated assumption maps, premortems or discovery-driven-planning checklists on decision quality; the core method has no direct LLM measurement.
agent_test: Build an assumption-map step and test it at equal tokens against plain reasoning.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM judges of business ideas agree poorly with experts on fine scores, and an LLM startup predictor reached only 26-50% accuracy on 50 firms (20% successes).
agent_test: Check that the agent abstains from forecasting venture success.

claim: The human Think-in-Opposites effect is large on the 2-4-6 task (success 78.3% vs 38.3% and 36.7%, N=180) but was shown on one task only; LLM gains are significant for thinking models and mixed for non-thinking ones.
agent_test: Compare a test-the-opposite prompt on thinking and non-thinking backbones on a business-assumption task.
audit_note: Human 78.3/38.3/36.7 and Qwen TiO table verified; the paper does mention prior DAX-MED work but its experiment is 2-4-6 only; LLM text 'mixed for non-thinking' matches (Qwen3-8B flat).

claim: A structured falsification agent with sequential error control (Popper) held Type-I error near the nominal 0.1 (0.082-0.103) with power 0.58-0.64, beating ReAct and Self-Refine, and ran about 10 times faster than 9 humans; 45% of its failed logs were test-design failures.
agent_test: Add a check that each proposed test could change the decision before running it.

claim: In one small study (Si et al., 43 executed NLP ideas) reviewer scores of LLM research ideas fell 1.98 points of 10 after execution vs 0.63 for human ideas, closing the pre-execution gap; separately, LLM-written business plans were rated 0.14 s.d. above entrepreneurs' originals by raters who had no outcome data (Csaszar et al., 10 plans), which shows LLM plans score well on pre-outcome ratings but does not itself show those ratings mispredict outcomes.
agent_test: Do not let the agent score its own plans as evidence; require a run or an external signal.
audit_note: Numbers verified (Si et al. 5.382 to 3.406 vs 4.596 to 3.968; Csaszar 0.14 sd), but the Csaszar result is rater scores of 10 plans with no tested outcome showing the scores were wrong, and Si et al. is a single small study (43 executed ideas, NLP only), so 'poor guide' is too general.
claim_before_audit: Reviewer scores before testing are a poor guide to tested outcomes: LLM research ideas lost 1.98 points (of 10) after execution vs 0.63 for human ideas; LLM business plans were rated 0.14 s.d. above entrepreneurs' plans without outcome data.

claim: Arguing a side raises LLM confidence rather than lowering it (debate: 72.9% to 83% mean, both sides at 75% or more in 61.7% of 60 debates); self-generated distractors with confidence normalisation cut calibration error on factual QA at about 10 calls. No premortem or devil's-advocate prompt has been measured on LLMs.
agent_test: Compare a premortem arm, a distractor-normalised arm and a plain arm on forecast calibration.

claim: Synthetic founder personas risk inflating optimism (polite lies) and have no tested predictive accuracy; no field study compares LLM-proposed cheap experiments with what founders ran.
agent_test: Use real behavioral signals for assumption tests, not simulated customers.
